Hacker Can Send Fatal Dose to Hospital Drug Pumps Email-ID 1078206 Date 2015-06-13 03:33:36 UTC From d.vincenzetti@hackingteam.com To list@hackingteam.it, flist@hackingteam.it

When security researcher Billy Rios reported earlier this year that he’d found vulnerabilities in a popular drug infusion pump that would allow a hacker to raise the dosage limit on medication delivered to patients, there was little cause for concern. Now Rios says he’s found the more serious vulnerabilities in several models of pumps made by the same manufacturer, which would allow a hacker to surreptitiously and remotely change the amount of drugs administered to a patient. “This is the first time we know we can change the dosage,” Rios told WIRED. The vulnerabilities are known to affect at least five models of drug infusion pumps made by Hospira—an Illinois firm with more than 400,000 intravenous drug pumps installed in hospitals around the world. The vulnerable models include the company’s standard PCA LifeCare pumps; its PCA3 LifeCare and PCA5 LifeCare pumps; its Symbiq line of pumps, which Hospira stopped selling in 2013 due to concerns raised by the FDA over other quality and safety issues with the pumps; and its Plum A+ model of pumps. Hospira has at least 325,000 of the latter model alone installed in hospitals worldwide. These are the systems that Rios knows are vulnerable because he’s tested them. But he suspects that the company’s Plum A+3 and its Sapphire and SapphirePlus models are equally vulnerable too. Hospira did not respond to a request for comment.

17 These things I command you, that ye love one another. - John 15:17 (KJV)

Jesus made it so very clear, that we were to love one another, and again He commands us to love one another. He commanded us to love one another as He has loved us (John 15:12). Jesus said that the greatest of all the commandments was to love God with all our hearts, and love our neighbor as ourselves (Mark 12:30-31). Jesus made it clear that all the law was fulfilled by these two commandments (Matthew 22:40). What an amazing thing it was for Jesus to take all the rules and regulations of the Old Testament Law, and sum them up in two commands of love – Wow!

This illustrates that all the things that were commanded for people to do under the law were just pictures of what love would have us do, if we would just love one another. So many Christians still don’t understand that under the New Testament Covenant that we have with God, we are not told we have to do works to be right with God, but we just have to love Him and others. The wonderful thing is that if you truly love God, and others, you will do all those things that were commanded under the law, but it will be done out of love, and not out of obligation. This takes all the pressure off of the Christian, if you understand this, and it does away with condemnation (Romans 8:1), which is the greatest tool that the devil uses against us. Praise God for making us a loving machine, instead of a doing machine.

Ok, so oatmeal is a cheap, filling meal that doesn't have to be boring. It can also be quick and convenient.

I've fallen in love with overnight oatmeal. It's a simple concept: mix oats and whatever else you like with milk and refrigerate it for 8 hours or so. In the morning you can eat it cold, or microwave it for a minute or two for a hearty, healthy, tasty meal. If you don't plan ahead you can use instant oatmeal or cooked oatmeal with the same ingredients. I thought I was crazy trying this in the middle of summer when it's over 90 degrees F where I live. But, today, my husband came in after working outside in the heat for most of the day and asked "can you make oatmeal? Or does it have to be done overnight?" I told him I would make something for him and I came up with my best flavor combo so far: Maple Bacon!

He's still raving about it and asking if I could make the bacon for other dishes! I plan to make this as an overnight oatmeal soon for him, but I can make it on request too.

Maple Bacon oatmeal:

Candied bacon: glaze cooked bacon with maple syrup and sprinkle with brown sugar. Broil one minute, repeat on other side.

Cut and sprinkle over oatmeal seasoned with a pinch of salt, a pat of butter, some brown sugar and maple syrup. Pour cream over oatmeal if desired,

Other "recipes"

All of these can be eaten cold or heated for about 2 min. You can add chia seeds or omit. I use about 1/3 cup oatmeal with an equal part milk. You can use soy, coconut or other milk. Or sub yogurt. Pour cream or half and half over to serve if desired.

My favorites so far for oatmeal:

Apple cinnamon cranberry raisin:

Add some chia seeds, Granny Smith Apple sliced thin (or sub dried apple) , a few golden raisins and some regular raisins and a few craisins (dried cranberry). A few pecans. Top with brown sugar and a pinch of salt.

Banana Bread oatmeal:

1/2 of a small mashed banana. Some chia seed. Mix in well with the oats. Add a few drops vanilla extract. A few walnuts and pecans. Top with brown sugar, and pinch of salt and a dab of butter, plus a few banana slices.

Cherry maple nut:

A few dried cherries, a couple of drops almond extract, about a tablespoon maple syrup, a sprinkle of brown sugar, some pecans, a dab of butter and a pinch of salt. Chia seed optional.

I'm planning to try some savory oatmeals next.
